test_title: RRB Technician Grade III Official Paper (Held On: 27 Dec, 2024 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: How long will it take for 1,500 to become Rs. 1,860 at 8% per annum simple interest?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total **Simple Interest** required = 1,860 − 1,500 = ₹360.

**Interest per year** = 8% of 1,500 = 1500 × (8/100) = ₹120.

**Time (T)** = Total Interest ÷ Interest per year = 360 ÷ 120 = 3 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 3 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Principal (P)** = ₹1,500

**Amount (A)** = ₹1,860

**Rate (R)** = 8% per annum

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e888968fcbbc8607c44a7d44af3c7eefca67acdb304fa23e60851d075d93a914.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

Amount (A) = P + SI

**Calculations:**

⇒ SI = A − P

⇒ SI = 1,860 − 1,500 = ₹360

⇒ 360 = (1,500 × 8 × T) ÷ 100

⇒ 360 = 15 × 8 × T

⇒ 360 = 120 × T

⇒ T = 360 ÷ 120

⇒ T = 3 years

**∴ The correct answer is 3 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Simple Interest (SI)

Calculated only on the **Principal** amount. SI = (P × R × T)/100 remains constant every year if P, R, and T are fixed.

Compound Interest (CI)

Interest calculated on the **Principal** plus **accumulated interest**. Formula: A = P(1 + R/100)T.

Rate of Interest (R)

The percentage of the principal charged as interest for a **specific period** (usually per annum).

1b8:Tbed
